# Independent HEAPS fixture and oracle design

This corpus freezes **25 acceptance cases and 38 concrete variants** for the H3
checkpoint. It contains independently authored synthetic records and literal
expected outcomes. It does not report H4 preparation or H5 runtime execution.
Passing the design tests checks the corpus, its byte bindings, its JSON Schema
specimens and its finite coverage. It does not establish that a consumer
implements the expected outcomes.

The fixture author is separate from the production schema author. The oracle
does not import production hashing, rendering or admission helpers. Its expected
dispositions are authored values in `oracle.json`, not results generated by the
implementation under assessment. Python's standard library independently
computes the frozen input identities; JSON Schema checks structural specimens.

## Corpus and provenance

`canonical/base-case.json` is an original safety-work1.1 case. Its seven
statements distinguish an observed document property, two conflicting accounts,
two alternative hypotheses, a proposed finding and a proposed recommendation.
The single factor is a candidate system condition. The mockup action is proposed
and its effectiveness remains pending evidence. No accepted clinical finding,
legal authority or organisational action is asserted.

Seven original synthetic text files are supplied:

| File | Role in the corpus |
| --- | --- |
| `sources/record.txt` | The supplied document contains a blank acknowledgement field; care omission is not established. |
| `sources/staff-account.txt` | One participant recalls a visible prompt. |
| `sources/consumer-account.txt` | Another participant recalls no visible prompt; the conflict remains unresolved. |
| `sources/synthetic-clock-rule.txt` | A fictional one-business-day target and explicitly defined UTC weekday calendar; no Queensland Health rule applicability. |
| `sources/record-summary.txt` | A derivative of the first source, retaining its source family. |
| `sources/record-revision-2.txt` | New bytes under the same source identity, used to challenge old bindings. |
| `sources/method-handover.txt` | A fictional prior-process to HEAPS decision that preserves previously supplied clocks. |

The base case consumes the first four sources. The summary, revision and method
handover are explicit scenario inputs. `source-manifest.json` records exact raw
UTF-8 byte hashes, lengths, source identities, revisions and family relationships.
The non-ASCII text in the record deliberately distinguishes UTF-8 canonical
hashing from an escaped-ASCII hashing domain. All names, times, events and
decisions are fictional. No official HEAPS form, patient data or restricted
instrument is reproduced. Original fixture text is covered by the repository
licence.

`packet/` contains literal structural input examples: a profile, original outline
and mapping, a hand-authored draft report, detached manifests and a simulated
draft decision. These are not generated H4 output vectors. The simulated decision
has unverified actual authority and no substantive approval; it exists to test
staleness. The status document is a schema specimen, not an observed validation
receipt.

## Literal variants and finite denominators

The catalogue contains four positive controls and 34 boundary or adversarial
variants. The expected preparation dispositions are **22 `prepare_draft`,
14 `reject_input`, and 2 `abstain`**. Independently, the expected review
dispositions are **31 `not_established`, 5 `stale`, and 2 `withheld`**.
These counts describe the authored oracle; they are not runtime pass counts.

| Acceptance case | Variants | Expected preparation boundary |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| HP01 | 1 | Prepare an explicitly synthetic draft. |
| HP02 | 1 | Reject a wrong case identity. |
| HP03 | 2 | Reject stale version or canonical hash. |
| HP04 | 2 | Reject wrong target kind or unresolved reference. |
| HP05 | 1 | Retain an unsupported recommendation as incomplete, without acceptance. |
| HP06 | 2 | Reject promotion using a withdrawn or rejected factor; preserve status. |
| HP07 | 1 | A correctly rebound revised report may be prepared; the old detached decision is stale. |
| HP08 | 1 | Preserve conflicting accounts and both unresolved alternatives. |
| HP09 | 3 | Missing, declined and unavailable participation do not establish consultation or agreement. |
| HP10 | 1 | Method selection establishes no protection, severity or reportability. |
| HP11 | 1 | Missing local template permits draft preparation, with conformity withheld. |
| HP12 | 2 | Reject replacement template or source bytes presented under old bindings; revalidation is required. |
| HP13 | 2 | Missing trigger or calendar leaves the deadline unresolved. |
| HP14 | 1 | A sourced fictional method handover preserves known and unknown clocks. |
| HP15 | 1 | An implemented action label does not establish effectiveness. |
| HP16 | 1 | A report without an external receipt establishes neither submission nor closure. |
| HP17 | 1 | Reject a non-synthetic label; all actual fixture bytes remain synthetic. |
| HP18 | 1 | A derivative adds a file but no independent source family. |
| HP19 | 1 | A documentation gap remains a gap, without a care-omission finding. |
| HP20 | 2 | Empty and all-withdrawn substantive inputs both withhold completed review. |
| HP21 | 3 | Replay, round-trip and object-key ordering preserve canonical and normalised values. |
| HP22 | 2 | Absent or unqualified optional AcciMap does not confer graph qualification or block the core draft. |
| HP23 | 1 | Incident, death-review and coronial questions remain distinct and open. |
| HP24 | 2 | Reject unknown fields or a malformed required version; no silent repair. |
| HP25 | 2 | Array or content changes alter canonical identity and invalidate old bindings. |

The 34 semantic rule IDs in `oracle.json` are a frozen evaluation vocabulary.
They are not claimed current CLI error codes. Each variant carries literal schema
expectations, semantic dispositions, required retained states, prohibited claims,
input hashes and explicit `h4: not_run` / `h5: not_run` fields.

## Materialising a variant

Start from the files named in `documents`, then apply `mutations` in order.
Every mutation has a target document, an `add` or `replace` operation, a path
array and a literal value. No automatic repair, rehashing or rebinding is implied:
any intentional new binding is already a literal mutation in the catalogue.

The `document_roles` field is mandatory. Documents marked `consumer_input` may
be supplied to a future harness. Documents marked
`illustrative_expected_status_not_input` are examples for schema design only.
They must never drive a consumer's preparation result, statement counts,
abstention or authorisation. Their hashes are nevertheless correctly rebound to
the illustrated profile so they do not introduce an unrelated stale-binding
defect.

`raw_artifact_overrides` deliberately supplies different raw bytes at an existing
bound slot. HP12 retains old profile and manifest hashes, so both template and
source replacements are integrity failures. A legitimate newly admitted revision
would require explicit new bindings and mapping revalidation; the harness must
not create that different arrangement through silent repair. HP07 supplies a
separate correctly rebound report manifest, isolating a stale prior decision.

## Count units and abstention

The count unit is **one canonical statement** in the bound case. Source files,
headings, factors, actions and status labels are not extra denominator items.
`input_items` includes statements retained for history. `usable_items` excludes
statements with `withdrawn: true` or a rejected/withdrawn provenance review state;
remaining eligibility is only for representation as the recorded epistemic kind,
not acceptance as a clinical fact. `abstained_items` retains explicit exclusion
reasons. For these classified fixtures, inputs equal usable plus abstained items.

HP20-empty supplies zero statements and no substantive entity references. Its
counts are 0/0/0. HP20-all-abstain preserves all seven statements and source
history, explicitly withdraws every statement and the linked factor, action and
review, and removes proposed finding/action presentation context. Its counts are
7/0/7. These input arrangements determine the expected result; the illustrative
status specimens do not.

## Canonical identity and packet-byte identity

The core fingerprint uses compact JSON with sorted object keys, preserved arrays,
unescaped Unicode and no final newline, encoded as UTF-8 and prefixed `sha256:`.
Normalised generated JSON uses sorted keys, two-space indentation, unescaped
Unicode and exactly one final LF. Both reject nonfinite values when serialised.
Raw input, source, template and manifest hashes bind exact bytes.

HP21 changes ingress representation in the round-trip and key-order variants.
Canonical and normalised case identity remain equal. Raw ingress bytes differ,
so an exact manifest that includes those ingress captures may also differ. No
approval over different raw bytes is presumed reusable. HP25 changes an array or
canonical content, so it must never retain the old canonical hash. This corpus
does not declare any canonical array semantically unordered and makes no blanket
semantic-equivalence claim for a permutation.

The acyclic specimen order is case/sources/template/mapping, then profile, then
report, then detached manifest, then separate simulated decision. The profile has
no own digest or later manifest/decision binding. Reports do not embed later
manifest or decision hashes. The final fixture lock is an inventory of design
artifacts and is not a HEAPS approval.

## Verification limits

Run `uv run --no-sync pytest -q tests/test_heaps_fixture_design.py` to check this
design. The test suite uses JSON Schema and standard-library operations; it never
invokes an H4/H5 public interface, renderer or packet admission implementation.
The separate core-validator check reported by the coordinator concerns only the
base canonical fixture.

The 38-variant denominator does not claim parser adversarial coverage for duplicate
JSON keys, malformed UTF-8, nonfinite values or unpaired surrogates. Those remain
explicit future H4 ingress tests. HP14 records an explicit synthetic method
handover; it does not qualify loading or migrating another production review
profile. Optional-component placeholders do not inherit component qualification.
No result establishes clinical validation, current local procedure applicability,
official form conformity, actual human acceptance or external submission.
